title: Not Your Father's UAW: Facebook Live and the 2023 UAW Strike
content: This paper explores the 2023 UAW Strike against the “Big Three” American automobile manufacturers and the union’s use of Facebook Live (FL) as a tool for organization and mobilization. Using John Kelly’s landmark Rethinking Industrial Relations Mobilisation, Collectivism and Long Waves (2012), the paper provides a short history of the 2023 strike and the difficulties faced by organized labor from the 1990s-2020. The UAWs use of Facebook Live (FL) in the strike is seen as bridging Kelly’s gap between organization and mobilization. The ubiquity of Facebook Live and livestream is seen as creating an environment in which union members can share information with each other, users can comment on aspects of the strike, and mainstream media outlets can access alternative views of the labor action. Facebook Live. Using Rainie and Wellman’s (2012) suggestion that Internet 2.0 platforms actually encourage and make it easy for users to work in virtual and real-life domains, the paper suggests that the sense of presence generated by Facebook Live helped the UAW to reach a good outcome. The use of FL in this labor action allowed for communication that helped the UAW to influence public opinion and increase membership. While recognizing that FL is not universally accepted across all users (Jung & Bhojwani 2025), the use of the platform by the UAW appears to have facilitated to some degree a settlement that was positive for the UAW.
